title: Dia De Los Muertos Selvedge - Indigo
description:
Dia De Los Muertos, a beautiful Mexican tradition honouring departed loved ones and guiding souls, is celebrated with a new Dia De Los Muertos Selvedge.

New artwork by the talented tattoo artist José Ruiz from Mexico City adorns the vegetable-tanned leather patch. His illustration depicts a skeleton guided by the Xoloitzcuintli, a sacred Mexican hairless dog believed to escort souls across a mystical river into the underworld. This motif, along with subtle iconography like agave plants, roots the design in Mexican tradition.

The heritage is woven into the fabric. This 12.5oz Japanese selvedge denim is made from 100% Mexican upland cotton, honouring its cultural origins. It’s woven in Okayama, Japan, on vintage shuttle looms using indigo rope-dyed yarns that will fade dramatically with wear. The selvedge ID, visible when you flip the cuff, features a playful multicolor stripe inspired by traditional Mexican sarape blankets.

Epperson Mountaineering
description:
Mark Epperson, a world-wise man who loves the mountains, founded Epperson Mountaineering in 1973 in Montana.  Mark’s vision back then is the same as it is today; he couldn’t find any other backpacks that satisfied his demanding need for high-quality packs.  He believed that by utilizing highest quality materials, artisan craftsmanship, and innovative functional designs he could make great backpacks which he could be proud of.  Thus, he ambitiously embarked on an unending quest to create the perfect backpack.

 Today, all Epperson Mountaineering products are still made in U.S.A. by artisan pack makers with the best components such as 1000 denier Cordura, YKK zippers, mil-spec tubular webbing or exclusive Indian/Oval pattern webbing, and reinforced seam-sealed inner compartments to guarantee long-term strength and durability.

 Honoring Mark’s wishes for everlasting quality, all Epperson Mountaineering products are continuously, individually scrutinized with careful attention to detail and persistent reflection of new ways to improve the ubiquitous backpack and other personal accessory products by Meg Company in California.

title: King Of Slub
description: The King of Slub is a 23oz Unsanforized Japanese Selvedge denim with an extremely slubby uneven texture. A result of low tension weaving techniques, and the use of custom developed irregular sized “King Slub Yarn”. The King Slub Yarn was developed over a 2 year period, as standard Slub yarns could not produce such an extreme three dimensional texture.  The yarn is rope dyed with indigo and due to the thickness and irregular shape of the yarn indigo absorption varies from section to section. Over time with wear, as the indigo starts to fade, a wide gradient of indigo becomes visible, and the thickness of the yarn allows for an extreme high contrast three dimensional textured fade.  Other details include, contrast stitching, classic red line selvedge id, buffalo leather patch, dark copper buttons and rivets.

title: Le Selvedge De La Belle Province
description:
Le Selvedge De La Belle Province is a 12.5oz Japanese Selvedge Denim inspired by Montreal, Quebec, the home of Naked & Famous Denim.  La Bell Province is the motto of Quebec, which in English translates to “The Beautiful Province”.  Within Canada, Quebec is distinct as it is a French speaking nation with its own unique naughty words – which you will find woven right into the selvedge.  You will also notice the fleur de lis along with the white and blue line selvedge id, representing the symbols and colors of Quebec.  The denim is woven using short slub irregular shaped yarns to give the fabric a gritty look.  The natural veg tanned leather patch features an alternative edition of the classic tragic blond logo with the words Denim Tout Nu & Celebre, French for Naked & Famous Denim as well as some nods to Montreal landmarks.  The artwork was created by local Montreal comic book artist Andy Belanger.  Other details include contrast stitching, and silver metallic buttons and rivets.

This jean was made to celebrate the hometown of Naked & Famous Denim and function as a special souvenir for those making the trip to Montreal.  This is why these jeans will not be available for purchase online, but will be exclusively available for in store purchase at Tate + Yoko, located at 9096 St. Laurent

Fabric Origin: Japan

title: New Rainbow Core Selvedge
description: The New Rainbow Core Selvedge is a 12.5oz Japanese selvedge denim that will fade to rainbow colors! The secret is in the dye method, traditionally rope dyed denim utilizes white cotton yarns which are repeatedly dipped in indigo such that the indigo dyes only coat the outermost layers of the cotton yarn. This leaves the center of the cotton yarn white. With wear and tear the indigo fades away and the white center core of the yarn is revealed. This is why your jeans fade from blue to white. The Rainbow Core denim is created by first dying yarns with permanent reactive dyes in all the colors of the rainbow. Then these colored yarns are rope dyed and coated with indigo, creating a yarn that is colored in the center with layers of indigo on top. As you wear the jeans the indigo will start to fade away and reveal their bright rainbow-colored center core. Cut, sewn, built in Canada with contrast stitching, a brown raging bull leather patch, along with silver metallic buttons and rivets.

description: When Irving Schott began making his elite line of leather jackets in the 1920s he called the collection "Perfecto", named after his favorite cut of cigar. title: Workforce Selvedge
description: Introducing the Workforce Selvedge, a 10.9oz lightweight Japanese selvedge denim that perfectly captures the essence of traditional workwear with its classic workwear blue tone.
